Adding a Redis cache at Qid cut our database load by 40%.

It's also the fix most likely to cause an incident a month later.

• Always set a TTL, even when you invalidate explicitly
• Add jitter so keys don't expire together
• Protect hot keys from cache stampedes
• Design for Redis being down

linkedin:
"Which message queue should we use?" really asks one thing: are you moving tasks, or recording events?

Tasks → RabbitMQ (or a Postgres jobs table)
Events → Kafka
Already running Redis and the volume fits in memory → Redis Streams

And whatever the docs say about exactly-once: make every consumer idempotent.
x: Kafka vs RabbitMQ vs Redis Streams in one line: tasks → RabbitMQ, events → Kafka, already-have-Redis → Streams.

My 6 steps:
1. Clarify requirements
2. Estimate scale
3. Define the API and data model
4. Sketch the high-level design
5. Deep-dive the hard parts
6. Cover failure modes and trade-offs
